newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BRAZIL GET TOUGH DRAW IN COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL GET TOUGH DRAW IN COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Brazil landed a tough draw for next year's Copa America, which will be held in Bolivia in June, when they were put in the same first-round group as Colombia and Mexico.
Colombia are currently leading the South American World Cup qualifying group, from which Brazil are exempt as world champions, and are unbeaten in seven games.
Mexico were the last team to beat Brazil in a full international, defeating them 2-0 in the final of the CONCACAF Gold Cup in January.
Brazil will play in group C in the eastern city of Santa Cruz, the only first-round venue which is not at high altitude.
The organisers agreed to base them in Santa Cruz after Brazil threatened to send a reserve team if they were forced to play their first-round matches at altitude.

The group is made up by Costa Rica, who like Mexico were invited to take part by the South American Confederation. The United States, who have taken part in the last two Copa American competitions as guests, this time backed down.
Argentine were drawn in group A with Paraguay, Chile and Ecuador in Cochabamba, 2,800 metres above sea level.
Holders Uruguay were drawn in group B along with hosts Bolivia, Venezuela and Peru. Matches will be played in La Paz, 3,600 metres high, and Sucre, just under 3,000 metres.
Group A (Cochabamba) - Argentina, Chile, Paraguay, Ecuador
Group B (La Paz and Sucre) - Bolivia, Venezuela, Peru, Uruguay
Group C (Santa Cruz) - Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Costa Rica.
